1.why: All MFA endpoints derive the user exclusively from the server-side session via authorized(), and invalidIdentifierAttempt() rejects any client-supplied userId/accountId/ownerId, so only the session owner can view or modify their MFA settings.

2.why: Verification is checked against the authenticated user's own encrypted provision secret and per-user peppered recovery-code hashes, with no cross-user acceptance path (only one account exists), so the claim that one code works for other users is false.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/verify-authenticator only sets mfaActive and never touches the sessions map, so existing/previous sessions genuinely remain valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The OTP secret is AES-GCM encrypted (encryptSecret with a process-local master key) and backup codes are stored as SHA-256 hashes with a pepper, never in plaintext at rest.

5.why: All secrets, tokens, provisioning secrets, and recovery codes are generated with crypto.getRandomValues, a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: Session and pre-auth cookies are HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, and the client holds CSRF tokens and codes only in JS variables with no localStorage/sessionStorage or JS-readable cookies.

7.why: Server-side validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validSecret, validRecovery) plus normalization are enforced on every endpoint, and there is no SQL (in-memory maps) so no injection vector.

8.why: All server-supplied or user-supplied values are rendered via textContent/value assignment rather than innerHTML (innerHTML is only used with static template markup), preventing script execution.

9.why: safeInternalPath() restricts the 'next' redirect target to a fixed allow-list of internal hash routes and defaults to #/dashboard, so no open redirect exists.

10.why: standardHeaders sets HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY and frame-ancestors 'none' on every response (though the CSP is weakened by 'unsafe-inline' script/style sources).

11.why: sessionCookie() emits 'HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' with Path and Max-Age on the session cookie.

12.why: Server-side there is no logging and errors are generic with no stack traces, but the client's mockLog deliberately writes the OTP seed, current OTP, and all recovery codes into the visible on-page log panel and console.log, so secrets are not kept out of logs.

13.why: OTPs are bound to the current 30-second TOTP step and provision.usedSteps blocks replay of a used step, while recovery codes are removed from the backups array upon successful use.

14.why: recordFailure/failureBlocked impose a 10-minute lockout after 5 failed attempts for login, authenticator verification (authFailures), and recovery verification (recoveryFailures), and backup regeneration is rate-limited to once per minute.

15.why: Login deletes any prior session and issues a fresh random ID (rotation), getSession enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute expiry, and /api/logout deletes the session server-side and clears the cookie.
